extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing responses to peer reviewers (researchers, academics submitting manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for authors on how to read, prioritize, draft, and submit organized responses to peer-reviewers and editors during manuscript revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consume reviewers’ critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Value feedback; avoid personalizing critiques; regard feedback as opportunities for improvement; address critiques systematically and patiently; remain composed and evaluate each comment objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should view feedback as valuable, not personal. Apply systematic review, patience, and reflection: categorize comments as major/minor, 'sleep on it' before replying, and avoid hasty responses. Transcend feelings of frustration and approach each comment neutrally, leveraging valid criticism to improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read carefully and understand the reviewers’ or editor’s comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly examine and categorize comments for clarity and understanding; break down comments into separate points; distinguish between positive feedback and critiques; address all points and number them accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully review the editor’s letter and each reviewer’s report to pinpoint emphasized points. Break complex comments into constituent issues. Number each comment, label them by reviewer (e.g., Review 1, comment 1), and evaluate whether and how each can be addressed. The objective is to demonstrate commitment by meticulously addressing every comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek opinion (Look for an opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult co-authors and colleagues to gain different perspectives; consult peers for feedback; brainstorm with the research group; reach consensus on addressing comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When uncertain how to address a comment, solicit input from co-authors, mentors, or field experts. Consider contacting the editor or a mentor for clarification. Group brainstorming can generate solutions for complex criticisms and help reach an authorial consensus on revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback dealing with requests for major revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on addressing major comments first, followed by minor ones; identify and prioritize major issues; revise and clarify significant points before attending to minor stylistic or grammatical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major comments typically concern scientific/methodological aspects (e.g., central hypothesis, main algorithm, redoing experiments). Minor remarks affect clarity or presentation (e.g., references, grammar, minor figures). Tackle major issues first as they can change conclusions; then address minor corrections without arguing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be polite and respectful of all reviewers / Express gratitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain professionalism and gratitude towards reviewers; regard reviewers’ comments as constructive; avoid confrontational or defensive tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start responses with thanks, avoid criticizing reviewer tone, and assume misunderstandings may stem from lack of clarity in the manuscript. If a reviewer misunderstands, apologize and clarify. Maintain a neutral, courteous tone even when refuting points. Consider acknowledging reviewers in the Acknowledgements section if their feedback substantially improved the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay attention to details: Respond to every point raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all points raised by reviewers are addressed individually; be specific in responses; include additional information if needed; make minor corrections to improve clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single bullet contains multiple issues, break it up and answer each subpoint. Provide requested data/figures or offer supplementary files if journal limits apply. You may delete or shorten material when necessary, specifying extent of reductions. Importantly, avoid copying reviewers’ comments verbatim into the manuscript — paraphrase suggestions in your own words to preserve originality and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thorough and plan responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and systematically respond to each comment; provide detailed, specific responses; number points and answer sequentially; ensure clarity and professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure responses formally (often by copying each reviewer comment and placing your reply under it). Start each reply with a clear direct answer (yes/no when feasible) and then explain changes. Tighten language, correct grammar, and indicate corresponding manuscript changes (page/line numbers). Comply with reviewer requests whenever feasible; where not, explain concisely why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t argue every single comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose your battles; only refute suggestions with valid reasons; provide rational explanations for disagreements; justify refusals concisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the reviewer before refusing. Provide factual, evidence-based justification when you decide not to implement a suggestion. Be aware reviewers may tolerate only a limited number of refusals; avoid protracted arguments. For substantial disputes that could jeopardize publication, appeal to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle unclear comments, conflicting feedback, and ethical concerns diligently; seek clarification for ambiguous comments; address conflicting feedback with a reasoned choice and explain to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For unclear remarks, ask the editor or request clarification in the cover letter. When reviewers contradict one another, choose the approach that best fits your vision and explain the rationale to the editor, outlining both comments. If you suspect ethical problems (e.g., reviewer misconduct, inappropriate citation requests, or undisclosed AI-assisted reviews), discreetly alert the editor and consult COPE/ICMJE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers’ requests vs journal guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers request additions (references, tables, text) that exceed the journal’s limits, authors should either implement with editor authorization or justify refusal using journal instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes improve the manuscript but exceed limits, seek editor approval and note this in responses. If changes conflict with your manuscript’s scope or journal rules, explain and justify your refusal referencing the journal’s author guidelines, and notify the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight changes in the revised manuscript - Use typography to assist the reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Make it easy for reviewers to see changes; detail responses and highlight significant modifications; consider typographical aids such as different fonts, colors, or track changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common methods include: (a) submitting a version with tracked changes, (b) highlighting edits, (c) using different colored text to link responses to changes, or (d) presenting a table with reviewer comments, author responses, and page/line references. Be mindful that colored fonts or heavy markup can make the manuscript long or hard to read; clarify your method in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a table format for responses (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table can include reviewer comments, author responses, and corresponding changes with page and line references in separate columns to improve clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tabular layout succinctly aligns each comment with the response and the exact manuscript location changed, facilitating verification by editors/reviewers. The article provides an Appendix (Table format) as an example. This format is widely recommended for clarity and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise and improve
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all necessary corrections are made and documented; highlight changes for easy verification; follow the journal’s submission requirements for revised versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check that the revised manuscript incorporates all claimed edits. If the journal asks for both a highlighted and a clean version, provide both. Verify formatting and adhere to the journal’s instructions to avoid delays or confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review again (final proofreading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a final thorough review to ensure no errors introduced by revisions; consider expert translators or AI proofreading but declare AI use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-native English authors should consider native-speaking editors or professional translation/proofreading. AI tools may assist with language but have limitations; use them as supplements and declare their use where required by journal policy. Do a final pass to ensure revisions did not introduce inconsistencies or mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express gratitude again (cover letter intro/conclusion and acknowledgements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude responses with gratitude to reviewers and editors; include an introductory paragraph expressing appreciation and a closing paragraph summarizing major changes and reiterating thanks; consider acknowledging reviewers if their feedback substantially improved the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the response letter with a brief thank-you and statement that each comment was considered. End with a summary of substantive changes and appreciation. Example intro: “The authors sincerely thank the reviewers for their thorough and insightful feedback... We have carefully considered each comment...” Consider adding reviewers to the paper’s Acknowledgements when their input materially improved the work (and if journal policy allows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmit promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmit the manuscript quickly with detailed responses and highlighted changes to keep the work fresh in reviewers’ and editor’s minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prompt, well-organized resubmission (response letter, response table, highlighted manuscript) demonstrates commitment and can increase acceptance likelihood. However, balance speed with thoroughness — do not rush and introduce errors.
